evals.name: message-from-staged-diff
evals.setup: A staged diff adding a JWT login endpoint: a new `handler/login.go` with `Login`, a `token.Issue` helper, and the route wired into the router. The conversation that produced it discussed session cookies at length — a design the diff does not contain.
expected_behavior: Derives the message from the diff alone — the session-cookie discussion never reaches the message
Summary line is imperative, lowercase, `feat(...)`-shaped, no trailing period, within ~50 chars
Defaults to `mini`: the summary plus one short paragraph wrapped at 72 columns that explains why, naming concrete symbols in backticks
Presents the message once in a zero-indent code block and stops — no `git commit` run or proposed, since the invocation did not ask for it

evals.name: amend-from-hash
evals.setup: `HEAD` is a commit whose message reads "fixes". Its diff corrects an off-by-one in a pagination cursor.
expected_behavior: Regenerates the message from that commit's own diff via `git show`, ignoring the staged diff
Amends with `git commit --amend` through a heredoc rather than creating a new commit, because the request asked for the amend
A bare `/cm <hash>` would only present the message — the amend happens on the explicit ask

evals.name: breaking-change
evals.setup: A staged diff removing the exported `Client.DoRequest` and folding its behaviour into `Client.Do`, with every internal caller updated.
expected_behavior: Marks the summary line with `!`
Carries a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer stating the impact and what callers must do instead
Uses no trailer other than `BREAKING CHANGE:` and `Refs:`

evals.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Opens with the message — no preamble and no narration of reading the diff
Presents the commit message once, in a zero-indent code block, and nothing else
Does not restate the diff or the message afterwards, and makes no unprompted offer to commit

evals.name: detail-matched-to-impact
evals.setup: A staged diff whose only effect is satisfying the linter: a package comment added, two identifiers renamed, one `#nosec` suppression. No behaviour changes.
expected_behavior: Summary line captures it as `style:` or `chore:`
Sums the cleanup in one sentence, or omits the body — it does not enumerate the mechanical edits one by one
Reserves per-symbol detail for changes a user of the software would notice; in a mixed commit those lead and the cleanup folds into one closing sentence

evals.name: verbosity-arguments
evals.setup: One staged diff, invoked twice at different verbosities.
expected_behavior: `micro` emits the summary line alone — no body, no footers, unless the change is breaking
`full` emits the summary plus a full-length multi-paragraph kernel-style body
The difference between them is length of body, not a different summary line

evals.name: apply-commits-without-confirming
evals.setup: A staged diff, with a harness attribution instruction active in the session asking for a `Co-Authored-By` trailer.
expected_behavior: Generates the message, then runs `git commit` through a heredoc without asking for confirmation
Honours the combined tokens: `micro apply` commits a one-line message
Adds no `Co-Authored-By` or other attribution trailer despite the active harness instruction
